shortDescription: Bluetooth headphones sound muffled, mono, or like a phone call in Call of Duty, Warzone, Discord, or OBS? Windows switched them to Hands-Free call mode. StereoKeeper brings stereo back in one click and can keep it that way. It sits in the tray, shows when your headphones drop into call mode and which app took the headset microphone, and restarts the headphone sound without changing Windows settings. Always stereo blocks the Hands-Free (HFP) profile for good if you talk through another microphone, and turning it off puts Windows back exactly as it was. For AirPods, Sony, Bose, Galaxy Buds, JBL, and any other Bluetooth headphones on Windows 11 and Windows 10. Free, no ads, no account.
description:
StereoKeeper fixes Bluetooth headphones that sound muffled, tinny, mono, or like a phone call on Windows 11 and Windows 10. It happens the moment Call of Duty voice chat, Discord, OBS Studio, or a Teams call turns on the headset microphone: footsteps go quiet, music loses its bass, and the sound often stays bad until you reconnect the headphones. StereoKeeper shows why it happened, names the app that took the microphone, and brings high-quality stereo back with one click.

Made for Call of Duty players. Warzone, Black Ops, and Modern Warfare open the headset microphone for in-game voice chat, sometimes as soon as the menu loads. Windows then switches your Bluetooth headphones to Hands-Free mode, and gunfire, footsteps, and positional audio turn flat right when you need to hear where the enemy is. Switch voice chat to another microphone or turn it off, then click Bring back stereo. If you play with a USB, laptop, or desk microphone, turn on Always stereo, and Windows can no longer drop your headphones into call mode at all. The same fix works for Helldivers 2, Counter-Strike 2, Roblox, and other games with voice chat.

Why your headphones sound like a phone call. Bluetooth headphones have two modes. A2DP plays high-quality stereo but has no microphone. The Hands-Free profile (HFP) carries the microphone but plays mono, low-quality sound made for calls; Windows shows it as Headset or Hands-Free AG Audio, and its switch in the device settings is called Hands-free Telephony. As soon as any app opens the headset microphone, Windows moves all sound to Hands-Free mode, so the game, the music, and the video you are watching sound compressed too. Windows 10 lists the two modes as separate Stereo and Hands-Free devices, and Windows 11 joins them into one device that switches by itself. Sometimes Windows does not switch back after the game or the call has ended.

Streamers and calls. OBS Studio, Discord, Microsoft Teams, Zoom, and Google Meet open the default Windows microphone, and if that is your headset, everything you hear turns mono. StereoKeeper warns you when the headphones are the default microphone, the most common reason they keep switching, and Bring back stereo ends the call mode that Windows forgot to end after a call.

See what is going on. The tray icon shows at a glance whether your headphones play in stereo, have dropped into call mode, or are protected by Always stereo. Click it, and the panel names every app that is using the headset microphone right now. Optional Windows notifications tell you the moment the sound turns mono and which app turned the microphone on.

Bring back stereo with one click. When the headphones are stuck in call mode, Bring back stereo restarts the headphone sound once, just as if you had reconnected the headphones, without changing any Windows settings. Call mode ends, the sound is stereo again, and the headset microphone keeps working for your next call. The panel shows every step live and even unsticks a Bluetooth hands-free service that stopped responding.

Always stereo for anyone with a separate microphone. If you talk through another microphone or do not need one at all, turn on Always stereo. It turns off the Bluetooth Hands-Free profile in Windows for all headphones at once, so no game or app can switch them to call mode again, and you always get full A2DP stereo with bass, detail, and positional audio. It does the job of unticking Hands-free Telephony by hand, except that the checkbox has to be cleared for each pair of headphones and often again after a reconnect, while Always stereo stays on until you turn it off. The switch is honest about the trade-off: while it is on, the headphones' own microphone does not work.

Safe and fully reversible. Before Always stereo changes anything, StereoKeeper remembers exactly how Windows was set up. Turn the switch off, and Windows goes back to precisely that state, with call mode allowed again. After every action the app checks the result, and the built-in help explains in plain words what each button changes and how to undo it. Windows asks for permission only when the app changes a setting; watching the headphones never needs it.

Works with your headphones. Sony WH-1000XM4 and WH-1000XM5, Bose QuietComfort, Apple AirPods, AirPods Pro and AirPods Max, Samsung Galaxy Buds, JBL, Soundcore, Jabra, Sennheiser, Beats, and gaming headsets used over Bluetooth: if Windows switches them to Hands-Free mode, StereoKeeper brings them back. A headset on its own USB dongle does not use Bluetooth and does not have this problem.

Light and private. StereoKeeper sits quietly in the tray with about 25 MB of memory, practically no CPU, and no graphics card use, so games keep every frame. No background service, no ads, no account, no telemetry, and no network connections: your data stays on your PC. Start with Windows, 30 interface languages picked from your Windows language, and a Copy info for the developer button that prepares a bug report with your user folder hidden.

Common questions. Why does the game sound bad only when voice chat is on? Voice chat opens the headset microphone, and Windows can use it only in Hands-Free mode. I use a separate microphone, so why does it still happen? Some app still opens the headset microphone, and the panel shows which one. Can I have stereo and the headset microphone at the same time? Not with classic Bluetooth; only LE Audio headphones on recent Windows 11 PCs can do both. Does StereoKeeper change drivers or sound settings? No. It installs no drivers and no audio effects; it only restarts or switches off the Windows Bluetooth hands-free services that decide between stereo and call mode. What should I do before uninstalling? Turn Always stereo off first, so Windows is back exactly as it was.

Works on Windows 11 and Windows 10 (version 2004 or later), on x64 and Arm PCs. StereoKeeper is free and open source under the MIT license, with the source code on GitHub. It is an independent app and is not affiliated with Activision, Discord, OBS Studio, or the makers of the games, apps, and headphones named here; their names belong to their owners.
